input:
You are knight_g1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 23. the team planned Nxb8 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Na5 instead, and that move was played, costing 508 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 9. the team planned c3 (pawn_c2), but queen_d1 (greed) sent Qxd5 instead, and that move was played, costing 790 centipawns.
- On move 13. the team planned Nf3 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Nh3 instead, and that move was played, costing 24 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only send your piece's move if the team's agreed plan names your piece and that exact move; if you see a capture or a threat to your piece that the plan ignores, say so in chat and wait for the team to re-plan instead of moving.
- Before sending a move, re-read the chat and confirm the plan names your exact piece and destination square (e.g., knight_g1 to f3); if you are not the named piece or the square differs, even if you see a capture or a threat, stay silent, post your concern in chat, and wait for the team to re-plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending your move, copy the plan's exact piece and destination square from the latest chat message and compare it character by character with the move you are about to send, and send it only if they match exactly; if they differ, or if you are not the named piece, send nothing and post your concern in chat instead.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
